title: Pekudei: Moses blessed them (Exodus 39:43)
hookLine: Moses sees the finished work and blesses the workers

lines: THE END OF A BIG JOB.
cards: The end of a big job has its own kind of quiet. A house renovated, a wedding pulled off, a school play performed, a garden finally planted. The people who did the work stand back, tired, a little proud, waiting.
And very often, nobody says anything. In the desert, the craftspeople bring every finished piece of the sanctuary to Moses: the tent, the ark, the curtains, the clothes. He looks it all over.
And then he does the thing so many finished jobs never get.

teach.b: In the JPS 1917 translation: "And Moses saw all the work, and, behold, they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, even so had they done it. And Moses blessed them." Three steps. He sees.
He recognizes that they did it right. And he blesses them. The rhythm has been heard before.
At the end of the sixth day of creation, Genesis says: "And God saw every thing that He had made, and, behold, it was very good."
Readers have noticed the echo, and more: the work is finished, the sanctuary completed, a blessing given, all language that recalls the creation of the world.
Some readers hear the building of the sanctuary told as a small creation, with Moses looking at it the way God looked at the world. What did he say? The verse doesn't tell us.

teach.h: MAY THE PRESENCE REST ON YOUR WORK.
teach.b: Rashi offers an answer from the midrash: Moses said, may it be God's will that the divine presence rest on the work of your hands.

teach.h: ESTABLISH THE WORK OF OUR HANDS.
teach.b: And Rashi connects it to Psalm ninety, which the Book of Psalms itself calls a prayer of Moses, and which ends by asking God to establish the work of our hands.
So the first thing Moses does with the finished sanctuary isn't to use it, or to correct it, or to move on.
It's to turn to the people who made it and bless them, and their hands.

how: Psalm 90, which the Book of Psalms calls a prayer of Moses, is among the psalms added on Shabbat and festival mornings in the traditional prayer book; Rashi ties its last verse, establish the work of our hands, to Moses' blessing here.

o: and Moses blessed them, the end of the building
the work of our hands, from a prayer of Moses
the accounts: the portion that finishes the sanctuary

games.q: what's inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: may the presence rest on your work

s: the Torah records the exact words of Moses' blessing
it only says he blessed them. Rashi offers what he may have said.
the end of the sanctuary story echoes the end of creation
saw, and behold, finished, blessed: readers have noticed it.
the Book of Psalms calls Psalm 90 a prayer of Moses
its opening line says so, and it ends with the work of our hands.

games.q: you're Moses. every piece of the sanctuary has been brought to you, finished. what's the first thing you do?
o: check it all, then bless the people who made it.
games.why: Moses saw all the work, and, behold, they had done it. and Moses blessed them.

practice: Think of something someone around you finished recently, a meal, a repair, a hard semester, and picture it the way Moses looked over every piece.
Notice what they did well, specifically, and the sentence that would show them you really saw it and wish good things for the work of their hands.

wordCard.voice: Pekudei. The portion where the work is finished, and Moses sees it, and blesses the people who made it.

orig.note: Hebrew: and Moses blessed them, the end of Exodus 39:43.

carryVoice: Your line: bless the workers. First he saw the work, then he blessed. See you tomorrow.
